Fluorine (F) has an atomic number of 9, meaning it has 9 electrons. When Li and F form an ionic bond to create LiF, lithium loses one electron to become Li⁺, and fluorine gains one electron to become F⁻. However, the total number of electrons is still the sum of the electrons in neutral Li and F atoms. Therefore, the total electron count of LiF is 3 + 9 = 12.
